question.text: Quaternary cytoreductive surgery in ovarian cancer: does surgical effort still matter?
question.context: To evaluate surgical outcome and survival benefit after quaternary cytoreduction (QC) in epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) relapse. We systematically evaluated all consecutive patients undergoing QC in our institution over a 12-year period (October 2000-January 2012). All relevant surgical and clinical outcome parameters were systematically assessed. Forty-nine EOC patients (median age: 57; range: 28-76) underwent QC; in a median of 16 months (range:2-142) after previous chemotherapy. The majority of the patients had an initial FIGO stage III (67.3%), peritoneal carcinomatosis (77.6%) and no ascites (67.3%). At QC, patients presented following tumour pattern: lower abdomen 85.7%; middle abdomen 79.6% and upper abdomen 42.9%. Median duration of surgery was 292 min (range: a total macroscopic tumour clearance could be achieved. Rates of major operative morbidity and 30-day mortality were 28.6% and 2%, respectively.Mean follow-up from QC was 18.41 months (95% confidence interval (CI):12.64-24.18) and mean overall survival (OS) 23.05 months (95% CI: 15.5-30.6). Mean OS for patients without vs any tumour residuals was 43 months (95% CI: 26.4-59.5) vs 13.4 months (95% CI: 7.42-19.4); P=0.001. Mean OS for patients who received postoperative chemotherapy (n=18; 36.7%) vs those who did not was 40.5 months (95% CI: 27.4-53.6) vs 12.03 months (95% CI: 5.9-18.18); P<0.001.Multivariate analysis indentified multifocal tumour dissemination to be of predictive significance for incomplete tumour resection, higher operative morbidity and lower survival, while systemic chemotherapy subsequent to QC had a protective significant impact on OS. No prognostic impact had ascites, platinum resistance, high grading and advanced age.

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates a significant survival benefit for patients undergoing quaternary cytoreductive surgery with complete tumor resection. The multivariate analysis highlights the predictive significance of multifocal tumor dissemination and the protective effect of postoperative chemotherapy. Therefore, surgical effort still matters.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: Mean OS for patients without vs any tumour residuals was 43 months (95% CI: 26.4-59.5) vs 13.4 months (95% CI: 7.42-19.4); P=0.001.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While the case focuses on ovarian cancer, other cancers with similar surgical approaches could be considered. However, the specific findings related to tumor resection and chemotherapy in this study are most relevant to the question of surgical effort in ovarian cancer.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that while quaternary cytoreductive surgery (QC) is associated with improved survival, the surgical effort alone does not significantly impact outcomes. The data shows that postoperative chemotherapy has a protective effect on overall survival (P<0.001), and multifocal tumour dissemination is a stronger predictor of survival than surgical outcome. The mean OS for patients with complete resection was 23.05 months, but this was significantly lower than the 43 months for those without any tumour residuals, indicating that residual disease post-surgery is the critical factor, not the surgical effort itself.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: The multivariate analysis showing that systemic chemotherapy subsequent to QC had a protective significant impact on OS (P<0.001) and that multifocal tumour dissemination was a stronger predictor of survival than surgical outcome.
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: No differential diagnoses needed to be considered as the question specifically addresses the role of surgical effort in QC outcomes, which is directly answered by the study's findings showing chemotherapy's greater impact than surgical effort.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that complete macroscopic tumour clearance (R0 resection) significantly improves overall survival (43 months vs 13.4 months), and postoperative chemotherapy further enhances survival (40.5 months vs 12.03 months). This strongly supports that surgical effort (i.e., achieving optimal cytoreduction) remains critical in quaternary cytoreduction for ovarian cancer.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: Mean OS for patients without any tumour residuals was 43 months vs 13.4 months for those with residuals (P=0.001), indicating that surgical effort directly impacts survival.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Considered whether chemotherapy alone or patient age/grade could explain survival differences, but multivariate analysis confirmed surgical resection completeness and chemotherapy as independent predictors, ruling out confounding factors.

olmo3_7b.critical_evidence: Mean OS for patients without any tumour residuals was 43 months vs 13.4 months for those with residuals (P<0.001).
olmo3_7b.differential_considered: Other factors like age, platinum resistance, and presence of ascites were not statistically significant prognostic markers in this study. The absence of residual disease remains the strongest predictor of survival, indicating that the primary importance is the quality of the resection, not just the effort or duration of surgery.
